column1: skm3-u1-uchini-while|Opportunity while a state lasts|学生のうちに、いろいろな国を訪ねたいです。|I want to visit various countries while I am a student.|Nのうちに sets a window that will end. The later action is something the speaker wants to do within it.

skm3-u1-uchini-while|Before a negative condition changes|忘れないうちに、予約の時間をメモしておこう。|I will write down the reservation time before I forget.|Vないうちに means while not yet forgetting: act before the condition changes.
skm3-u1-uchini-while|Adjective attachment|温かいうちに食べてください。|Please eat it while it is warm.|An い-adjective attaches directly. The intended action should occur before the food cools.

skm3-u1-uchini-change|Gradual development|毎日話すうちに、緊張しなくなりました。|As I spoke every day, I gradually stopped feeling nervous.|Repeated activity continues while a change develops; this is not an instruction to seize an opportunity.
skm3-u1-uchini-change|Unnoticed change|気づかないうちに、外は暗くなっていました。|It had become dark outside without my noticing.|The negative form is also possible. The change happened while the speaker was unaware.
skm3-u1-aida-vs-aidani|Ongoing situation across a span|子供が寝ている間、私は本を読んでいました。|I was reading while my child slept.|間 frames two continuing activities over the relevant interval.

skm3-u1-aida-vs-aidani|Event within that span|子供が寝ている間に、夕食を作りました。|I prepared dinner while my child was asleep.|間に locates the preparation/completion within the sleep period. It need not take only an instant.
skm3-u1-aida-vs-aidani|Noun attachment|留守の間に、荷物が届きました。|A parcel arrived while I was away.|Nの間に: an arrival occurs within a period of absence.

skm3-u1-te-kara-denaito|Decision requires prior information|実物を見てからでないと、買うかどうか決められません。|I cannot decide whether to buy it until I see the actual item.|The second clause expresses inability to decide before the prerequisite.

skm3-u1-te-kara-denaito|Negative meaning without a negative verb|許可をもらってからでなければ、入場は無理です。|Entry is impossible until permission has been obtained.|無理 is negative in meaning although it does not end in ない. Do not demand a particular negative ending.
skm3-u1-tokoro-da-phases|About to start|今から夕食を作るところです。|I am just about to make dinner.|Dictionary form + ところ locates the moment just before the action starts.

skm3-u1-tokoro-da-phases|In progress, caught in the act|こっそりお菓子を食べているところを、妹に見られました。|My younger sister saw me secretly eating sweets.|Vているところを marks the ongoing scene as the object of 見る. It is not simply a sentence-final ところだ.

skm3-u1-tokoro-da-phases|Just completed, then an event|宿題が終わったところで、友達から電話が来ました。|Just as I finished my homework, a friend called.|Vたところで gives the stage at which another event occurred. This is different from concessive Vたところで meaning even if.

skm3-u1-tokoro-da-phases|Arrival into a situation|料理ができたところへ、お客さんが来ました。|The guests arrived just as the food was ready.|ところへ fits an arrival into the situation; the following verb determines the particle.
skm3-u2-toori-ni-accordance|Following what was demonstrated|先生がやったとおりに、紙を折ってください。|Please fold the paper the way the teacher did.|Vたとおりに refers to an already demonstrated model.
skm3-u2-toori-ni-accordance|Noun and voiced form|予定どおりに、会議は三時に始まりました。|The meeting began at three as scheduled.|Nどおり is voiced. With の, use Nのとおり: 予定のとおり.
skm3-u2-ni-yotte-variation|Different people, different outcomes|好きな食べ物は人によって違います。|Favorite foods differ from person to person.|によって marks the variable across which the result changes.
skm3-u2-ni-yotte-variation|Some specific cases|店によっては、現金しか使えません。|At some shops, only cash can be used.|によっては singles out some cases rather than making a claim about every shop.
skm3-u2-tabini-repetition|Verb trigger|この曲を聞くたびに、学生時代を思い出します。|Every time I hear this song, I remember my student days.|Dictionary verb + たびに links each occurrence to the recurring response.
skm3-u2-tabini-repetition|Noun trigger, routine result|出張のたびに、報告書を書きます。|I write a report each time I go on a business trip.|Nのたびに. A recurring result need not be emotional or surprising.
skm3-u2-ba-hodo-proportion|Verb correlation|練習すればするほど、動きが自然になります。|The more I practice, the more natural my movements become.|Repeat the same verb in conditional and dictionary forms.
skm3-u2-ba-hodo-proportion|Adjective correlation|荷物は軽ければ軽いほど、運びやすいです。|The lighter the luggage, the easier it is to carry.|い-adjective: ければ + dictionary adjective + ほど.

skm3-u2-ba-hodo-proportion|Na-adjective correlation|説明は簡単なら簡単なほど、分かりやすいです。|The simpler the explanation, the easier it is to understand.|The adjective before ほど uses な. The first conditional can also be expressed with であれば.

skm3-u2-tsuide-ni-opportunity|Secondary task during a planned trip|銀行へ行くついでに、郵便局にも寄ります。|While I am going to the bank, I will also stop at the post office.|The bank visit is the main purpose; the post-office stop is an added convenience.

skm3-u2-tsuide-ni-opportunity|Completed main action|部屋を掃除したついでに、窓も拭きました。|While I was at it after cleaning the room, I wiped the windows too.|Vたついでに can refer to the opportunity created by doing the main task.
skm3-u3-kurai-hodo-extent|Degree illustrated by a possible action|声が出ないくらい驚きました。|I was so surprised that I could not speak.|くらい gives a concrete indication of the degree of surprise.

skm3-u3-kurai-hodo-extent|Hyperbolic comparison|昨日は倒れるかと思うほど疲れました。|Yesterday I was so tired that I thought I might collapse.|ほど can express an extreme degree without saying the comparison event actually happened.

skm3-u3-kurai-wa-nai|Subjective superlative|私には、家で休むほど幸せな時間はありません。|For me, no time is as happy as resting at home.|A negative comparison expresses a subjective highest evaluation, not a measured universal fact.
skm3-u3-kurai-wa-nai|Related comparison with は|今日は昨日ほど寒くありません。|Today is not as cold as yesterday.|XはYほど…ない compares two items. This is not necessarily a superlative among all items.

skm3-u3-kurai-nara|Rejecting an undesirable option|そんなに長く待つくらいなら、別の店に行きます。|Rather than wait that long, I will go to another shop.|The speaker judges waiting to be the worse option and chooses an alternative.

skm3-u3-kurai-nara|Preference despite the alternative's cost|嫌な仕事を続けるくらいなら、収入が減っても転職したいです。|Rather than continue a job I dislike, I want to change jobs even if my income falls.|The alternative need not be ideal; it is preferred to the rejected situation.
skm3-u3-ni-kagiru|Noun recommendation|暑い日は冷たい麦茶に限ります。|On a hot day, nothing beats cold barley tea.|Nに限る gives a subjective best choice, not an access restriction.
skm3-u3-ni-kagiru|Affirmative action|疲れたときは、早く寝るに限ります。|When you are tired, the best thing is to go to bed early.|Dictionary verb + に限る recommends an action.
skm3-u3-ni-kagiru|Negative action|体調が悪いときは、無理をしないに限ります。|When you feel unwell, it is best not to push yourself.|Vない + に限る recommends refraining from the action.
skm3-u4-hanmen-flipside|Two aspects of one thing|この部屋は日当たりがいい反面、夏は暑くなります。|This room gets good sunlight, but on the other hand it becomes hot in summer.|One feature has both a benefit and a drawback.
skm3-u4-hanmen-flipside|Coexisting feelings|新しい生活が楽しみな反面、不安もあります。|I am looking forward to my new life, but I also feel anxious.|The two feelings coexist; な-adjective + な反面.
skm3-u4-kawari-ni-exchange|Substitution|今日は母のかわりに、私が料理を作ります。|Today I will cook instead of my mother.|Nのかわりに replaces a person in a role.
skm3-u4-kawari-ni-exchange|Compensation or trade-off|この仕事は大変なかわりに、給料が高いです。|This job is demanding, but the pay is high in return.|な-adjectiveなかわりに balances a drawback with compensation.

skm3-u4-kawari-ni-exchange|Exchange between actions|買い物を手伝うかわりに、日本語を教えてください。|In return for my helping with the shopping, please teach me Japanese.|The first action is offered in exchange for the second.

skm3-u4-ni-taishite|Contrast between subjects|兄は静かなのに対して、弟はよく話します。|My older brother is quiet, whereas my younger brother talks a lot.|A clause is nominalized with の before に対して. This compares different subjects.
skm3-u4-ni-taishite|Target rather than contrast|この店の店員は客に対して親切です。|The staff at this shop are kind toward customers.|Nに対して identifies the target of an attitude; it does not mean in contrast to here.
added-n3-4-46|One aspect alongside another|この町は便利な一方で、家賃が高いです。|This town is convenient, while rents are high.|な-adjective + な一方で links coexisting aspects.
added-n3-4-46|Reformulating a description|彼は怒っているというより、困っているようです。|He seems troubled rather than angry.|というより replaces a less accurate description with a more fitting one.
skm3-u5-tame-ni-causality|Cause and unfavorable result|大雪のため、電車が遅れています。|Trains are delayed because of heavy snow.|Nのため identifies a cause. This is not a purpose someone intends to achieve.

skm3-u5-tame-ni-causality|Cause versus purpose|事故があったために、道路が通行止めになりました。|The road was closed because there had been an accident.|Past factual clause + ために gives a cause; compare a deliberate purpose such as 留学するために貯金する.
skm3-u5-koto-kara-origin|Reason behind a name|桜の木が多いことから、この通りは桜通りと呼ばれています。|This street is called Sakura Street because it has many cherry trees.|An observed fact explains how a name arose.

skm3-u5-koto-kara-origin|Evidence for an inference|電気が消えていることから、店は閉まっていると判断しました。|From the fact that the lights were off, I judged that the shop was closed.|ことから identifies the evidence supporting a judgment, not just a personal excuse.

skm3-u6-no-dakara-reality|Known premise supporting advice|明日は試験なのだから、今夜は早く寝たほうがいいです。|Since you have an exam tomorrow, you should go to bed early tonight.|Nなのだから treats the premise as relevant and supports advice.

skm3-u6-no-dakara-reality|Premise supporting an expectation|十年も住んでいたのだから、この町に詳しいでしょう。|Since they lived here for ten years, they probably know the town well.|The conclusion can be an expectation, not only a command. Tone can make the reminder sound insistent.
skm3-u5-okage-sei|Favorable attribution|友達が手伝ってくれたおかげで、早く終わりました。|Thanks to my friend's help, I finished early.|The speaker evaluates the effect positively and attributes it to the help.
skm3-u5-okage-sei|Unfavorable attribution|夜更かししたせいで、授業中眠くなりました。|Because I stayed up late, I became sleepy during class.|せいで attributes an unwanted result; the blamed cause can be one's own action.
added-n3-5-47|Cause with a noun|台風によって、多くの家が被害を受けました。|Many houses were damaged by the typhoon.|によって identifies the cause of the damage.
added-n3-5-47|Modifying a noun|地震による被害を調べています。|We are investigating damage caused by the earthquake.|による modifies the following noun; によって normally connects to a predicate.

skm3-u6-tewa-dewa-negative-consequence|Problematic action as a condition|毎晩そんなに遅く寝ては、体に悪いですよ。|If you go to bed that late every night, it is bad for your health.|ては introduces a condition evaluated negatively in the following clause.
skm3-u6-tewa-dewa-negative-consequence|Unsuitable state|この字では、小さすぎて読めません。|With writing like this, it is too small to read.|Nでは presents the existing condition as inadequate for the desired result.
skm3-u6-sae-ba|One sufficient condition|住所さえ分かれば、荷物を送れます。|As long as I know the address, I can send the package.|さえ highlights the condition the speaker treats as sufficient.

skm3-u6-sae-ba|Verb-stem attachment|毎日練習しさえすれば、少しずつ上達します。|As long as you practice every day, you will gradually improve.|V-stem + さえすれば emphasizes carrying out the action. It expresses the speaker's assessment, not a universal guarantee.
skm3-u6-tatoe-temo|Hypothetical obstacle|たとえ雨が降っても、試合は行います。|Even if it rains, the match will go ahead.|The assumed obstacle does not change the stated decision.
skm3-u6-tatoe-temo|Noun predicate|たとえ無料でも、必要のない物はもらいません。|Even if something is free, I will not take it if I do not need it.|Nでも forms the concession; it is not Nても.

added-n3-6-48|Premise raised by the listener|京都へ行くなら、この地図を持っていってください。|If you are going to Kyoto, take this map with you.|なら takes the proposed trip as a premise. The map is taken before or during the trip; なら does not mean after.
added-n3-6-48|After a condition is fulfilled|駅に着いたら、電話してください。|Please call when you arrive at the station.|たら permits a request triggered after arrival.
added-n3-6-48|General condition|時間があれば、参加します。|If I have time, I will participate.|A stative ば condition can accompany the speaker's intention. Do not ban intentions after every ば clause.

added-n3-7-49|Relaying a message|受付の人によると、面接は三階で行うとのことです。|According to the receptionist, the interview will be held on the third floor.|とのことだ formally relays information from a source; it is not a claim of direct observation.

added-n3-7-49|Reported information with a noun predicate|案内によると、参加費は無料だということです。|According to the notice, participation is free.|A noun predicate retains だ before reported ということだ. 案内によると identifies the information source.
added-n3-7-50|A generally reported view|この町は住みやすいと言われています。|This town is said to be easy to live in.|The source is a general body of opinion rather than a named speaker.
added-n3-7-50|Report is not proof|その建物には百年の歴史があると言われていますが、資料は残っていません。|The building is said to have a hundred-year history, but no records remain.|と言われている reports a claim without proving its truth.
added-n3-7-51|Tentative hearsay|田中さんは来月引っ越すとか。|I hear Tanaka is moving next month.|Sentence-final とか can relay something heard with a tentative tone; it differs from listing examples with NとかNとか.
added-n3-7-51|Casual report|店は今日は休みだって。|I heard the shop is closed today.|って is a casual reporting form here; the noun predicate has だ.
added-n3-7-51|Naming a person|鈴木さんという人から電話がありました。|There was a call from someone named Suzuki.|という links a name to a following noun. This naming use is different from a full reported proposition.

skm3-u8-to-wa-kagiranai-not-necessarily|Rejecting a universal generalization|高い物が必ずしも長持ちするとは限りません。|Expensive things do not necessarily last a long time.|Some may last, but the price does not guarantee that result.

skm3-u8-to-wa-kagiranai-not-necessarily|Frequency is not universal|週末だからといって、いつも暇だとは限りません。|Just because it is the weekend does not mean I am always free.|The negation targets an assumed generalization; it does not mean I am never free.

skm3-u8-nai-koto-wa-nai-litotes|Qualified possibility|一人でできないことはないですが、時間がかかります。|It is not impossible to do it alone, but it will take time.|The double negative acknowledges possibility while keeping a reservation.

skm3-u8-nai-koto-wa-nai-litotes|Qualified evaluation|おいしくないことはないけれど、少し高いです。|It is not that it is not tasty, but it is a little expensive.|An い-adjective negative can form the same qualified affirmation.

skm3-u8-wake-ga-nai|Strong inference from evidence|まだ五歳なのだから、こんな難しい本が読めるわけがありません。|Since the child is only five, there is no way they can read a book this difficult.|The speaker rejects the possibility based on a premise; this expresses the speaker's reasoning, not independently verified impossibility.
skm3-u8-wake-ga-nai|Noun predicate|あの人が犯人のわけがない。|That person cannot possibly be the culprit.|Nのわけがない is a strong denial. である can also link a noun in a more formal style.

skm3-u8-wake-dewa-nai|Rejecting an inference|嫌いなわけではありませんが、今日は食べたくありません。|It is not that I dislike it, but I do not want to eat it today.|The speaker denies the inferred reason, not the factual refusal to eat.
skm3-u8-wake-dewa-nai|Partial scope|全部分かったわけではありません。|It is not that I understood everything.|The negative applies to understanding everything. Some parts may have been understood.

added-n3-8-52|Admit an action, add a reservation|読んだことは読みましたが、細かいところは覚えていません。|I did read it, but I do not remember the details.|The verb is repeated with matching tense; the first clause concedes the action.

added-n3-8-52|Admit a quality, qualify its importance|安いことは安いですが、駅から遠いです。|It is cheap, certainly, but it is far from the station.|The adjective is conceded, then another consideration limits the endorsement.
added-n3-9-53|Want someone else's action|先生に作文を見てもらいたいです。|I would like my teacher to look over my essay.|に marks the person whose help is desired; もらいたい frames receiving the favor.
added-n3-9-53|Desired action or state|子供には健康でいてほしいです。|I want my child to stay healthy.|てほしい states the speaker's desired situation for someone else, not that person's own desire.

added-n3-9-53|Want someone not to do something|ここでは写真を撮らないでほしいです。|I would like people not to take photos here.|Vないでほしい requests the absence of an action. Tone and relationship affect how direct it sounds.

added-n3-9-54|Seeking permission for one's action|会議で私にも意見を言わせてもらいたいです。|I would like to be allowed to express my opinion at the meeting too.|The speaker wants permission to perform the causative-marked action, not to make the listener speak.

added-n3-9-54|More deferential wording|事情を説明させていただきたいのですが。|I would like to be allowed to explain the circumstances.|いただきたい is more deferential than もらいたい. Permission/benefit must fit the situation; the phrase is not a universal politeness decoration.
added-n3-9-55|Hope for another person|旅行の日、晴れるといいですね。|I hope it is sunny on the day of your trip.|といい can express a wish about something outside the speaker's direct control.
added-n3-9-55|Hope for oneself|来年、日本へ行けたらいいなと思っています。|I am hoping I can go to Japan next year.|The potential 行ける makes the desired possibility clear. たらいい is not limited to giving advice.
added-n3-9-55|Wishing a condition held|もう少し時間があればいいのですが。|I wish I had a little more time.|ばいい can express a wish; context distinguishes this from a suggestion about what to do.

skm3-u9-beki-da|Advice based on a norm|間違いに気づいたら、すぐに訂正すべきです。|If you notice a mistake, you should correct it promptly.|べき expresses what the speaker judges appropriate; it is stronger than a neutral prediction.

skm3-u9-beki-da|Negative advice|人の秘密を勝手に話すべきではありません。|You should not disclose someone else's secrets without permission.|べきではない advises against the action. It is different from saying the action is physically impossible.
added-n3-10-56|Direct imperative|危ない！止まれ！|Watch out! Stop!|The imperative can be appropriate in an urgent warning; in ordinary requests it may sound forceful.
added-n3-10-56|Direct prohibition|ここに入るな。|Do not enter here.|Dictionary verb + な is a direct prohibition, not the explanatory な used before の.

added-n3-10-56|Written instruction|提出前に、名前を確認すること。|Check your name before submitting.|Sentence-final こと is used for written rules/instructions. It is not a conversational request in the same register as ください.
added-n3-10-56|Negative written instruction|試験中は辞書を使わないこと。|Do not use a dictionary during the exam.|The negative clause before こと gives a written prohibition.

added-n3-10-57|Suggest a possible solution|一度、先生に相談してみたらどうですか。|Why not try consulting your teacher once?|The past-form shape is part of the suggestion construction, not a report that consultation already happened.

added-n3-10-57|Tone can make advice critical|そんなに疲れているなら、少し休んだらどう。|If you are that tired, why not rest a little?|Tone determines whether the suggestion sounds caring or impatient; it is not automatically polite in every relationship.

skm3-u11-you-to-suru-inception|Attempt that fails|ドアを開けようとしましたが、鍵がかかっていました。|I tried to open the door, but it was locked.|The volitional form plus とする indicates an attempt; it does not guarantee success.
skm3-u11-you-to-suru-inception|On the point of happening|電車が発車しようとしています。|The train is about to depart.|This use describes an imminent event, not a personal intention belonging to the train.

skm3-u11-you-to-suru-inception|Refusal/lack of willingness|何度頼んでも、彼は話そうとしません。|No matter how often I ask, he will not try to speak.|ようとしない describes a lack of willingness or attempt, rather than ordinary inability.
skm3-u7-you-ni-suru|Deliberate effort|忘れ物をしないように、出かける前に確認します。|I check before going out so that I do not forget anything.|The negative clause specifies the outcome the speaker tries to avoid.
skm3-u7-you-ni-suru|Habitual effort|毎日少しでも歩くようにしています。|I make an effort to walk at least a little every day.|ようにしている presents ongoing effort; it does not claim perfect success on every occasion.
skm3-u11-koto-ni-shite-iru|Personal rule|夜十時以降は仕事のメールを見ないことにしています。|I make it a rule not to check work email after ten at night.|ことにしている presents a policy chosen and maintained by the speaker.

skm3-u11-koto-ni-shite-iru|A settled routine|毎月、給料の一部を貯金することにしています。|I make it a practice to save part of my salary every month.|Compare ようにしている, which emphasizes trying to maintain the behavior rather than declaring the rule itself.

skm3-u11-tsumori-da|Belief versus reality|十分説明したつもりでしたが、伝わっていませんでした。|I thought I had explained it adequately, but it had not got across.|Vたつもり expresses the speaker's belief about what they had done, not a future intention.
skm3-u11-tsumori-da|Imagined role|先生になったつもりで、この問題を説明してください。|Explain this problem as if you were the teacher.|つもりで asks someone to adopt an imagined role for the action.
skm3-u12-keigo-respect|Respecting the actor|先生はもうお帰りになりました。|The teacher has already gone home.|お + verb stem + になる honors the teacher's action, not the speaker's.
skm3-u12-keigo-respect|Respecting a guest|お客様はロビーでお待ちになっています。|The guest is waiting in the lobby.|The honorific form is about the person being respected, not simply anyone older than the speaker.
skm3-u12-keigo-humble|Action directed toward someone respected|資料は私がお届けします。|I will deliver the materials.|お届けする humbles the speaker's action toward its recipient.

skm3-u12-keigo-humble|Humble action with a recipient|先生に研究の結果をご報告しました。|I reported the research results to my teacher.|ご + suitable suru-noun + する. Prefix choice and whether the pattern is idiomatic must be learned with the expression.

added-n3-12-58|Politeness toward the listener|私は山田と申します。|My name is Yamada.|申す presents the speaker's saying politely toward the listener; not every humble verb needs a person as the action's destination.
added-n3-12-58|Humble/polite movement report|明日は九時に参ります。|I will come/go at nine tomorrow.|参る is a humble/polite counterpart of 行く/来る; choose come versus go from the situation.
added-n3-12-58|Polite existence|受付は一階にございます。|The reception desk is on the first floor.|ございます is a polite form of ある. It does not honor the desk as an actor.
added-n3-a-59|Also and even|子供も大人も参加できます。|Both children and adults can participate.|も adds each group; it is not the only-use sense of しか.
added-n3-a-59|Exclusion with a negative|今日は千円しか持っていません。|I have only one thousand yen today.|しか excludes amounts beyond this and pairs with a negative predicate.
added-n3-a-59|Approximation|駅まで十分くらいかかります。|It takes about ten minutes to the station.|くらい gives an approximate quantity here, not an extreme degree comparison.
added-n3-a-59|Unexpected inclusion|先生までその冗談を聞いて笑いました。|Even the teacher laughed at that joke.|まで adds an unexpected case. It does not mark an endpoint in time here.
added-n3-b-60|Topic|日本の教育について調べています。|I am researching education in Japan.|について introduces the topic being investigated.
added-n3-b-60|Target|店員は客に対して丁寧に説明しました。|The shop assistant explained politely to the customer.|に対して marks the target of the explanation/attitude.
added-n3-b-60|Evaluating viewpoint|私にとって、この写真は大切です。|This photograph is important to me.|にとって identifies whose standpoint supports the evaluation.
added-n3-b-60|Role|通訳として会議に参加しました。|I attended the meeting as an interpreter.|として states a capacity or role, not an evaluation.
added-n3-c-61|General action as a topic|毎日運動することは大切です。|Exercising every day is important.|こと nominalizes the activity as an abstract topic.
added-n3-c-61|Perceived event|子供が公園で走っているのを見ました。|I saw a child running in the park.|の is natural for an event directly perceived with 見る; do not substitute こと mechanically.
added-n3-c-61|Concrete thing|何か冷たいものが飲みたいです。|I would like something cold to drink.|もの refers to a thing; it is not interchangeable with nominalizing の/こと here.
added-n3-d-62|Resemblance|この雲は魚のように見えます。|This cloud looks like a fish.|Nのように compares appearance; it does not express purpose.
added-n3-d-62|Goal|後ろの人にも聞こえるように、大きな声で話しました。|I spoke loudly so that people at the back could hear too.|A non-volitional/potential outcome precedes purpose ように.
added-n3-d-62|Indirect instruction|先生は、来週までに読むように言いました。|The teacher told us to read it by next week.|ように introduces the content of an instruction. It is not resemblance or a purpose clause here.
skm3-u7-you-ni-purpose|Potential outcome|日本語の新聞が読めるように、漢字を勉強しています。|I am studying kanji so that I can read Japanese newspapers.|The goal is an ability expressed with the potential form.

skm3-u7-you-ni-purpose|Negative outcome to avoid|電車に遅れないように、早く家を出ました。|I left home early so that I would not miss the train.|Vないように is natural for avoiding an unwanted result; it does not require a potential verb.

skm3-u8-wake-niwa-ikanai|Situational obligation against an action|明日は大切な試験なので、今夜は遊ぶわけにはいきません。|I have an important exam tomorrow, so I cannot go out for fun tonight.|The obstacle is what is appropriate or responsible, not physical inability.
skm3-u8-wake-niwa-ikanai|Double negative obligation|約束したので、行かないわけにはいきません。|Since I promised, I have to go.|The negative verb reverses the practical conclusion: not going is unacceptable.
added-n3-e-63|Reasoned conclusion|毎日三時間練習しているのですか。上手なわけですね。|You practice three hours every day? That explains why you are good.|わけだ connects new information with an understandable conclusion.

added-n3-e-63|Obligation from a double negative|代表に選ばれたので、出席しないわけにはいきません。|Since I was chosen as representative, I have to attend.|ないわけにはいかない expresses an obligation. It does not mean impossible to attend.
added-n3-f-64|Only or predominantly|弟は甘い物ばかり食べています。|My younger brother eats almost nothing but sweet things.|Nばかり describes a strong bias toward one category.
added-n3-f-64|Repeated behavior|休みの日は寝てばかりいます。|On days off I do nothing but sleep.|Vてばかりいる focuses on repeated/excessive behavior, often with criticism.
added-n3-f-64|Not only|この店は安いばかりでなく、量も多いです。|This restaurant is not only cheap; the portions are large too.|ばかりでなく adds a second favorable feature here.

added-n3-f-64|Subjectively recent completion|先月始めたばかりなので、まだ慣れていません。|I only started last month, so I am not used to it yet.|たばかり can count last month as recent relative to the activity; it does not always mean a few seconds ago.

added-n3-f-64|Only a final action remains|準備は終わりました。あとは出発するばかりです。|The preparations are finished. All that remains is to leave.|Dictionary verb + ばかり describes a remaining action here; it is not the worsening-trend use.

added-n3-g-65|Deliberate change versus change in state|部屋を明るくしました。窓を開けると、もっと明るくなりました。|I made the room brighter. When I opened the window, it became brighter still.|する focuses on making the change; なる presents the resulting change.

added-n3-g-65|Chosen decision versus arrangement|私は参加することにしました。会議は金曜に行うことになりました。|I decided to participate. It has been arranged that the meeting will be held on Friday.|ことにする emphasizes a decision; ことになる presents the settled outcome without necessarily identifying the decision-maker.
added-n3-g-65|Developing ability|練習して、泳げるようになりました。|After practicing, I became able to swim.|ようになる describes a change in ability/habit, not simply deciding to do it.

skm3-u11-koto-ni-natte-iru|Standing rule|この学校では、上履きを履くことになっています。|At this school, students are required to wear indoor shoes.|ことになっている reports an established rule or arrangement rather than the speaker's personal policy.
skm3-u11-koto-ni-natte-iru|Scheduled arrangement|会議は十時に始まることになっています。|The meeting is scheduled to begin at ten.|The arrangement can be a schedule, not only a prohibition or institutional rule.
added-n3-h-66|Actual discovery|窓を開けると、庭に猫がいました。|When I opened the window, there was a cat in the garden.|Narrative と can describe an actual past discovery, not only a natural law.

added-n3-h-66|Unexpected situation after action|駅に着いたら、電車はもう出ていました。|When I reached the station, the train had already left.|たら locates an actual discovery after arriving; the train's departure happened earlier.
added-n3-h-66|Adding two features|この店は料理もおいしければ、サービスもいいです。|This restaurant has both good food and good service.|も…ば…も lists coexisting features rather than setting an if-then condition.
added-n3-i-67|Not necessarily|有名な店が必ずしもおいしいとは限りません。|A famous restaurant is not necessarily good.|必ずしも combines with a negative scope, not a universal positive assertion.
added-n3-i-67|Emphatic negative|このことは決して忘れません。|I will never forget this.|決して strengthens the negative predicate.
added-n3-i-67|Resemblance|まるで夢を見ているようです。|It feels as though I am dreaming.|まるで pairs naturally with an expression of resemblance such as ようだ.
skm3-fj-ppoi-personality|Resembling a quality|この服は少し子供っぽいです。|These clothes look a little childish.|Nっぽい means having a perceived quality. The evaluation often depends on context.

skm3-fj-ppoi-personality|Tendency with a verb stem|最近、忘れっぽくなりました。|Recently I have become forgetful.|V-stem + っぽい forms an adjective for a tendency; its attachment is lexical, not freely available with every verb.
skm3-fj-darake-flaws|Covered with an unwanted substance|転んで、服が泥だらけになりました。|I fell and my clothes became covered in mud.|Nだらけ commonly describes an undesirable substance or condition spread throughout.
skm3-fj-darake-flaws|Many defects in an abstract thing|この文章は間違いだらけです。|This passage is full of mistakes.|だらけ also applies to flaws, not just physical dirt.
skm3-fj-gachi|Repeated tendency|忙しいと、朝食を抜きがちです。|When I am busy, I tend to skip breakfast.|V-stem + がち describes a recurring tendency, often considered undesirable.
skm3-fj-gachi|Noun attachment|子供のころは病気がちでした。|I was often ill as a child.|Nがち occurs with established combinations such as 病気がち; do not attach it to every noun indiscriminately.
skm3-u10-rashii|Information-based inference|彼は来月引っ越すらしいです。|Apparently he is moving next month.|Plain clause + らしい expresses an inference or information received indirectly.
skm3-u10-rashii|Typical quality|今日は春らしい暖かい日です。|Today is a warm, springlike day.|Nらしい means characteristic of that noun; it is not hearsay about spring.
added-n3-j-68|Onset and continuation|雨が降り始めて、一時間ほど降り続きました。|It started raining and continued for about an hour.|V-stem + 始める and 続ける distinguish starting from continuing.
added-n3-j-68|Sudden onset|赤ちゃんが急に泣き出しました。|The baby suddenly started crying.|出す often highlights a sudden onset; 始める is a more general start.
added-n3-j-68|Completion|長い小説をやっと読み終わりました。|I finally finished reading the long novel.|終わる marks completion of the activity.
added-n3-j-68|Doing completely|一人で全部食べ切りました。|I ate it all by myself.|切る emphasizes completing the action fully or exhausting its object.
added-n3-j-115|Partly completed|机の上に飲みかけのお茶があります。|There is some partly drunk tea on the desk.|V-stem + かけ describes something started but unfinished.

added-n3-j-115|Persistence through completion|最後まで自分の意見を言い通しました。|I maintained my opinion all the way to the end.|通す emphasizes persisting through the whole course, rather than merely reaching an endpoint.
added-n3-j-115|Subjective difficulty|このことは家族にも話しづらいです。|This is difficult to tell even my family.|づらい often highlights personal discomfort or difficulty; compare neutral difficulty with にくい.

added-n3-p2-1-124|Keep quotation boundaries|先生は「明日は休みです」と言いました。|The teacher said, “Tomorrow is a day off.”|と closes the quoted message and attaches it to 言う; the quoted sentence can retain polite style.

added-n3-p2-1-124|Embedded question versus assertion|先生に、明日は休みかどうか聞きました。|I asked the teacher whether tomorrow was a day off.|かどうか marks a yes/no question embedded as the content of 聞く. Do not assemble it as a quotation asserting the answer.

added-n3-p2-2-125|Find the head noun|昨日駅で会った人から、メールが来ました。|I received an email from the person I met at the station yesterday.|昨日駅で会った modifies 人. The following から marks that whole noun phrase as the source.
added-n3-p2-2-125|Keep the modifying clause's subject|妹が作ったケーキを、みんなで食べました。|We all ate the cake my younger sister made.|妹が belongs inside the modifier; ケーキを is the object of the main predicate 食べました.
added-n3-p2-3-126|Content of a noun|試験の日が変わったという知らせを聞きました。|I heard the news that the exam date had changed.|という links a proposition to a noun describing its content; 知らせ is the main noun before を.
added-n3-p2-3-126|Representative examples|京都や奈良といった町を訪ねました。|I visited cities such as Kyoto and Nara.|といった presents examples of the following category. The list need not be exhaustive.

added-n3-p2-4-127|Keep the whole fixed form|一度読んだだけでは、全部理解できません。|I cannot understand everything after reading it only once.|だけでは belongs together before the negative conclusion. Ordering fragments requires the complete construction.

added-n3-p2-4-127|Place modifiers before the noun|日本語を勉強し始めたばかりの学生です。|This is a student who has only just started studying Japanese.|勉強し始めたばかり modifies 学生 through の; retain the verb-suffix chain in order.

added-n3-p3-1-131|Topic and final predicate agree|私がこの町を選んだ理由は、交通が便利だからです。|The reason I chose this town is that its transport is convenient.|The topic 理由は needs a reason predicate; the intervening clause must not make you lose track of that structure.

added-n3-p3-1-131|A cause introduced by なぜなら|この町に住みたいです。なぜなら、職場に近いからです。|I want to live in this town because it is close to my workplace.|なぜなら introduces the explanation; からです completes the expected reason construction.
added-n3-p3-2-132|Reference time in past narration|駅に着いたとき、雨が降っていました。|It was raining when I reached the station.|ていました presents the ongoing situation at the past arrival time.

added-n3-p3-2-132|Earlier change, continuing result|駅に着いたとき、店はもう閉まっていました。|When I reached the station, the shop had already closed.|The closing happened earlier; ていました describes the resulting closed state, not ongoing closing.

added-n3-p3-3-133|Event without a stated agent|窓が開いていました。寒かったので、私が閉めました。|The window was open. It was cold, so I closed it.|開く is intransitive; 閉める is transitive. The second sentence omits the understood object 窓を.

added-n3-p3-3-133|Agent and object|私がコップを割ってしまいました。割れたコップは捨てました。|I accidentally broke a glass. I threw away the broken glass.|割る takes the object; 割れた modifies the resulting broken item. Follow the same participant across sentences.
added-n3-p3-4-134|Approach to a reference point|友達がこちらへ歩いてきました。|My friend walked toward me.|くる views the movement toward the speaker's reference point.

added-n3-p3-4-134|Development over time|日本語が少しずつ分かってきました。これからも勉強していきます。|I have gradually come to understand Japanese. I will keep studying from now on.|てきた connects development to now; ていく projects continuation away from now into the future.

added-n3-p3-5-135|Passive experiencer|弟に大切な本を汚されて、困りました。|My younger brother got my important book dirty, which caused me trouble.|The omitted subject is the affected speaker; に marks the person who dirtied the book.

added-n3-p3-5-135|Causative and causative-passive viewpoints|先生は学生に作文を書かせました。学生は作文を書かされました。|The teacher made the students write an essay. The students were made to write it.|The same event is viewed from the causer and then from those made to act. Particle roles and the subject change.

added-n3-p3-6-136|Giver's action toward the speaker|友達が道を教えてくれました。それで、迷わずに着きました。|A friend showed me the way, so I arrived without getting lost.|くれる presents the friend's action as a benefit toward the speaker's side.
added-n3-p3-6-136|Receiver's viewpoint|私は友達に道を教えてもらいました。|I had a friend show me the way.|もらう makes the receiver the subject; に identifies the person giving the help.

added-n3-p3-7-137|Reference to an object|新しい机を買いました。その机は窓のそばに置きました。|I bought a new desk. I put it beside the window.|その机 refers back to the previously introduced desk; the second sentence omits the subject 私.

added-n3-p3-7-137|Reference to a whole event|電車が遅れました。それで、会議に間に合いませんでした。|The train was delayed. Because of that, I did not make it to the meeting on time.|それ refers to the preceding situation as a cause, not merely to the noun 電車.

added-n3-p3-8-138|Introduce a subject, then continue its topic|庭に猫がいます。その猫は毎朝ここに来ます。|There is a cat in the garden. That cat comes here every morning.|が introduces the cat in the existence statement; は then presents it as the continuing topic.
added-n3-p3-8-138|Identify who answers the question|誰が説明しますか。私が説明します。|Who will explain? I will.|が identifies the requested person. This focus differs from introducing a general topic with は.

added-n3-p3-9-139|Contrast despite an expectation|雨が強くなりました。それでも、試合は続きました。|The rain got heavier. Even so, the match continued.|それでも presents continuation despite a circumstance that could have stopped it.

added-n3-p3-9-139|Restatement rather than cause|この部屋には誰もいません。つまり、今は使われていません。|There is nobody in this room. In other words, it is not being used now.|つまり reformulates the point; choose it from the logical relation, not from a shared word.

added-n3-p3-10-140|Consistent narration|この町は静かです。公園も多く、住みやすいです。|This town is quiet. It also has many parks and is easy to live in.|The surrounding narrative maintains polite endings while an internal connective clause need not end in です.

added-n3-p3-10-140|A quotation can have a different style|彼は「明日は行かない」と言いました。私は驚きました。|He said, “I am not going tomorrow.” I was surprised.|Plain speech inside a direct quote is compatible with polite surrounding narration. Do not mechanically change quoted speech.
